summary: This TypeScript handbook-style note explains narrowing, the process by which TypeScript refines a declared union type to a more specific type based on type guards, assignments, and control flow. It walks through typeof checks, truthiness narrowing (including pitfalls with null and empty strings), equality narrowing, the in and instanceof operators, assignments, control flow analysis, user-defined type predicates, and assertion functions. The note ends by introducing discriminated unions using a Shape type with circle and square kinds.
one_line: A TypeScript handbook guide to narrowing, covering type guards, control flow analysis, type predicates, and discriminated unions.
key_facts: TypeScript refines types to more specific types than declared through a process called narrowing.
A check such as typeof padding === "number" is called a type guard in TypeScript.
The typeof operator in TypeScript is expected to return one of eight strings: string, number, bigint, boolean, symbol, undefined, object, function.
typeof null returns "object" in JavaScript, so checking typeof strs === "object" alone leaves null in the narrowed type string[] | null.
Values that coerce to false in truthiness checks include 0, NaN, "" (the empty string), 0n, null, and undefined.
The double-Boolean negation !!"world" has the narrow literal type true, while Boolean("hello") is inferred as type boolean.
Equality narrowing with x == null removes both null and undefined from the type.
With the in operator, optional properties appear on both sides of the narrowing check.
instanceof narrowing checks whether the prototype chain of x contains Foo.prototype.
Assignments narrow the observed type of a variable, but assignability is checked against the declared type.
Control flow analysis lets TypeScript remove number from string | number after an if block that returns when padding is a number.
A user-defined type guard uses a type predicate return type of the form parameterName is Type.
Using zoo.filter(isFish) with a Fish | Bird array yields a Fish[] array.
The Shape interface with kind, radius, and sideLength optional fields fails to tell the type checker which fields are present for each kind.
The note recommends a discriminated union, with Circle (kind "circle", radius number) and Square (kind "square", sideLength number), as a better encoding.
